engine.definition: The machine in a vehicle that produces power to move it.
engine.exampleUsage: The engineer inspected the engine that supplied mechanical power.

transmission.definition: A system that transfers power to a vehicle’s wheels and provides the required drive ratios or modes.

clutch.definition: A mechanism that connects or disconnects an engine from the transmission.

carburetor.definition: A device in some engines that mixes fuel with air before combustion.

spark-plug.definition: An engine component mounted in the cylinder head produces a high-voltage spark that ignites the mixture of air and fuel.

piston.definition: A moving part inside an engine cylinder that helps transfer power.

crankshaft.definition: A shaft that converts the pistons' movement into rotation.

camshaft.definition: A rotating shaft that controls when an engine's valves open and close.

turbocharger.definition: A device driven by exhaust gases that forces extra air into an engine to increase its potential power.
turbocharger.exampleUsage: The mechanic inspected the turbocharger for signs of damage.

exhaust.definition: The gases released by an engine, or the pipe that carries them away.

hood.definition: The hinged cover over a car's engine compartment.

trunk.definition: Compartment in an automobile that carries luggage or shopping or tools.
trunk.exampleUsage: She put the luggage in the car’s trunk.

bumper.definition: A part fitted to the front or rear of a vehicle to help absorb minor impacts.

fender.definition: A barrier that surrounds the wheels of a vehicle to block splashing water or mud.

roof.definition: The top outer part of a vehicle's body.

windshield.definition: Transparent screen (as of glass) to protect occupants of a vehicle.

side-mirror.definition: A mirror mounted on the side of a vehicle so the driver can see areas beside and behind it.
side-mirror.exampleUsage: The driver adjusted the side mirror before moving.

headlight.definition: A front vehicle light designed to illuminate the road ahead.

taillight.definition: Lamp (usually red) mounted at the rear of a motor vehicle.

dashboard.definition: The panel in front of the driver that contains instruments and controls.

steering-wheel.definition: The wheel the driver turns to control a vehicle's direction.
steering-wheel.exampleUsage: The licensed driver adjusted the steering wheel position before the journey.

gear-shift.definition: A lever or control used to select a vehicle's transmission gear or driving mode.
gear-shift.exampleUsage: The gear shift was in the parking position.

pedal.definition: A foot-operated control used to accelerate, brake, or operate the clutch.

seat-belt.definition: A vehicle restraint designed to help hold an occupant in place during sudden movement or a collision.

airbag.definition: An inflatable vehicle safety device designed to help cushion an occupant during specified impacts.
airbag.exampleUsage: The instructor explained that an airbag supplements the seat belt.

glove-box.definition: A storage compartment built into the dashboard area of a vehicle.

console.definition: The section between the front seats that holds controls and storage.

sun-visor.definition: A movable shade above a vehicle’s windshield used to reduce direct glare.

rearview-mirror.definition: An interior vehicle mirror providing a view behind the vehicle.

tire.definition: A rubber covering around a wheel that grips the road.

wheel.definition: A simple machine consisting of a circular frame with spokes (or a solid disc) that can rotate on a shaft or axle (as in vehicles or other machines).
wheel.exampleUsage: The technician inspected the wheel separately from the tire.

rim.definition: The outer part of a wheel to which the tire is attached.

hub-cap.definition: A cover fitted over the central part of a vehicle wheel.
hub-cap.exampleUsage: One hub cap was loose and needed to be secured.

brake-pad.definition: A friction component pressed against a brake disc to slow wheel rotation.

brake-disc.definition: A metal disc attached to a wheel that brake pads press against to slow the vehicle.
brake-disc.exampleUsage: The mechanic measured the brake disc for wear.

shock-absorber.definition: A mechanical component in a vehicle’s suspension absorbs energy from bumps, vibrations, and sudden impacts. By limiting repeated bouncing, it makes the ride smoother and helps the vehicle remain stable.

spring.definition: An elastic metal part that compresses or stretches to absorb forces.

axle.definition: A shaft on which a wheel rotates.

alignment.definition: The adjustment of wheel angles so the vehicle travels as intended.

engine-oil.definition: Lubricating oil used inside an engine to reduce friction and help protect moving parts.
engine-oil.exampleUsage: The service record shows when the engine oil was last changed.

coolant.definition: A fluid that carries heat away from an engine to help prevent overheating.

brake-fluid.definition: Hydraulic fluid that transfers pressure through a vehicle's braking system.
brake-fluid.exampleUsage: A technician checked the brake-fluid level during maintenance.

transmission-fluid.definition: A specialized fluid used to lubricate, cool, or operate parts of a vehicle transmission.
transmission-fluid.exampleUsage: The mechanic checked the transmission-fluid condition.

windshield-washer.definition: A vehicle system that sprays cleaning fluid onto the windshield to help the wipers remove dirt.
windshield-washer.exampleUsage: The windshield washer sprayed fluid across the glass.

power-steering-fluid.definition: Hydraulic fluid used in some power-steering systems to assist steering movement.
power-steering-fluid.exampleUsage: The technician inspected the power-steering-fluid reservoir.

gas.definition: Gasoline used as fuel in a vehicle's engine.

diesel.definition: A type of fuel used in diesel engines.

battery-acid.definition: A sulfuric-acid electrolyte used in lead-acid batteries, rather than in every type of rechargeable battery.

refrigerant.definition: A substance that carries heat through an air-conditioning system.

door.definition: A movable panel used to open or close an entrance.
